direction.premise: A microscope for mathematical emergence: local rules are instruments and the evolving geometry, not the controls, is the hero.
direction.composition: A nearly full-height black mineral observation chamber, narrow scientific switchboard above and a shallow transport desk below; dual worlds contract the chamber into two synchronized specimens.
direction.shapeLanguage: Hard-edge square cellular pixels and precise rectangular controls; a small diamond cross marks the four-neighbor avalanche without decorative cards.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Dry ceramic and basalt scientific apparatus: flat muted surrounding alloy, inset charcoal observation glass and sparse metallic etched typography, without glassmorphism.
direction.paletteLogic: Muted gray chalk surrounds the experiment; mineral pigments identify cell states while amber marks changing controls; alternative palettes preserve color-state distinctions.
direction.typography: Compact functional sans for actions, engineering monospace for live step counters and rules, and restrained serif only within the explanatory laws sheet.
direction.signature: One tap buds a second real universe from the precise same simulation state, changes one local law, and renders both specimens progressing side by side.
direction.distinction: KASKAD's older particle-forces workshop is a scene builder; this sibling exposes three exact discrete mathematical automata. Press has a document-processing rail and Bzyn has a launcher toy; neither is a doubled mathematical specimen.

architecture.primaryVerb: Create an actual cell-state rule system, paint or mirror its initial condition on the specimen, and fork/rewind the result under alternate laws.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Ink appears in the exact painted lattice cells immediately, real rules change synchronous transitions, and the historical checkpoint restores full cell and parameter arrays.
architecture.spatialRationale: An unframed dark square microscope expands between the mode rail and control desk; only in authoring mode a tactile physical brush tray docks below it. Forking keeps paired live specimens.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Glyad is a relief-editing optical illusion with a height painter and stereogram output, whereas this instrument keeps a black live pixel-cell microscope and docks a compact state-ink tray inside the stage only during editing.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Glyad hides edited terrain as a static depth illusion; the Kaskad editor assigns discrete transition laws and evolves, forks, saves and rewinds truly changing automata cells.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Skol Siege centers an authored medieval castle and a tactile trebuchet on an organic landscape; this app is a mathematically generated square pixel microscope that can duplicate vertically into two specimens.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Skol Siege involves pointing a siege weapon at stone targets and watching destruction; this app changes automata parameters, injects cells and compares evolving rule-derived patterns.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Press splits a physical file-work ledger and operation rail, while this app is a continuous, mostly unframed scientific observation chamber.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Press batches bytes into encoded outputs; this app modifies mathematical cell laws and evolves live dual universes under touch.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Bzyn features a tall framed spring toy with a red projectile; this product presents square pixel fields that become vertically paired microscope specimens.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Bzyn fires and catches a physical puck; this app feeds automata, edits neighbor rules, saves exact lattice states and forks experiments.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Folkarium arranges a manuscript score in a wide editable folio; here a dark square scientific specimen takes almost all attention.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Folkarium authors pitches and synthesizes music; this app evolves local cellular rules without notes or a timeline.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Sin Guion has a spoken quiz station with dense language prompts; this app is a single live mathematical surface with minimal text.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Sin Guion evaluates oral exercises while this app branches persistent simulation worlds and produces animated GIF evidence.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rivals DNA uses consecutive dossier pages and rating lists; this surface has no questionnaires, panels or deck navigation.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Rivals DNA ranks selected heroes; here a user injects local perturbations, changes diffusion constants and compares outcomes.

production.renderer: Three deterministic pure-JavaScript model engines produce compact cell arrays; Canvas ImageData displays genuine state with crisp sand/ant pixels and organic reaction interpolation.
production.focalAsset: A four-way toppling-cell motif in bespoke app-local SVG source and final icon, together with a live zero-asset computational field.

motion.character: Continuous mathematically derived change inside a fixed chamber with immediate precision inputs, not bouncing cards or ambient oscillation.
motion.action: A single branch button turns one uninterrupted world into two side-by-side evolving specimens without losing the original state.
motion.anticipation: The pressed branch control depresses instantly and the new chamber space is calculated before both representations are painted.
motion.response: Two exact copies appear immediately; the mutant fork receives one changed parameter and thereafter follows its own real computation.
motion.followThrough: Subsequent frames display divergence from the same initial state, and independent taps add local changes to the selected world.
motion.interruption: All pointer input targets the current world instance, cancellation ends painting, and continuous animation pauses on hidden tabs.
motion.reducedMotion: The simulation remains legible as sequential still states; nonessential modal movement is disabled when reduced motion is requested.

evidence.expectedChange: A second world specimen is visible and the interface displays two independently evolving mathematical grids after the branch action.
